replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse (brute force, mass signup, email/SMS flooding, scraping): design has no sign-in or public form — only "Sales staff upload customer lists as CSV files" and a summary email to the uploader; no mass-messaging or public endpoint stated. Not applicable.
- Staff/admin screens rendering other people's content: design never states any screen or page that renders imported values — only "written straight into the customers table" and "export customers back to CSV". Not applicable (the one-reviewer stored-XSS item depends on an unstated rendering surface).
- Privileged actions without a record: present — "Rows from the CSV are written straight into the customers table" — already covered by listed threat 7.
- Personal pages/documents cached by browsers or CDNs: design states no download page, headers or CDN; only "The CRM can export customers back to CSV". Not applicable.
- Attacker text reaching spreadsheets, emails, logs, other systems: present — "export customers back to CSV" (covered by listed threat 3) and "emails the uploader a summary" (covered by listed threat 6).
- One-reviewer items: upload/drop-location has no stated authentication or role check ("Sales staff upload customer lists as CSV files. A nightly job loads each file") — real and not covered by any listed threat. The other one-reviewer items (id overwrite, stored XSS) are duplicates of listed threat 5 or depend on unstated rendering.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["CSV upload", "nightly import job", "CRM customers table", "summary email", "CSV export for marketing"],
    "dataStores": ["customers table", "uploaded file store"],
    "externalServices": ["email"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["sales staff -> upload store", "upload store -> nightly job -> CRM database"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "No authentication or role check stated for who may submit files the nightly job trusts",
      "scenario": "The design names only 'Sales staff' as uploaders and describes no authentication or authorisation on the upload path, nor any check that a file the nightly job picks up came from a legitimate uploader. Any internal user, contractor, compromised host or internal service that can reach the upload path or write into the location the job reads can plant a CSV. The job loads it straight into the customers table as if sales had submitted it, and emails a summary, so attacker-supplied records enter the CRM with a legitimate-looking origin.",
      "component": "CSV upload path / nightly import job file intake",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Sales staff upload customer lists as CSV files. A nightly job loads each file into the CRM database and emails the uploader a summary." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing in the design checks that the person or system handing over a customer file is actually allowed to, so anyone inside can get rows into the CRM.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate and authorise every import submission",
        "given": "a CSV file awaiting the nightly import",
        "when": "the job selects the file for loading",
        "then": "it only processes files submitted through an authenticated upload by a principal holding the sales-import role, records that principal with the file, and rejects or quarantines files with no verified submitter"
      }
    }
  ]
}
